s: Government monitoring of phone and internet records should be tightly limited, even if some attacks become harder to stop.
I lean toward limiting monitoring to protect privacy, even at some cost to security.
I lean toward allowing broad monitoring for security, even if innocent people's records are collected.
Broad monitoring to catch terrorists and spies should be allowed, even if many innocent people's records are collected.
surveillance_tradeoff.torn: I weigh privacy and security about equally here.

s: Intelligence agencies should always need a judge's warrant before reading Americans' messages, even if it slows investigations.
I lean toward requiring a warrant first, even if investigations slow down.
I lean toward letting agencies collect first and get approval later.
Agencies should be able to collect Americans' messages first and get approval afterward, so threats aren't missed.
warrant_tradeoff.torn: I weigh getting a warrant first and moving fast about equally.

s: Police and city cameras and plate readers should be kept to a minimum, even if some crimes go unsolved.
I lean toward fewer public cameras, even if some crimes go unsolved.
I lean toward more public cameras, even if more of people's movements are recorded.
Police and city cameras and plate readers should be used widely, even if everyone's movements are recorded.
cameras_tradeoff.torn: I weigh fewer cameras and more cameras about equally.

encryption_access: Tech companies shouldn't have to build a way for police to unlock encrypted phones or messages, even with a court order.
Companies should have to help police unlock encrypted devices only in the most serious cases, like terrorism or child exploitation, with a court order.
Companies should have to give police a way to unlock encrypted devices in any criminal case with a court order.
facial_recognition: Police should be banned from using facial recognition.
Police can use facial recognition only to identify suspects in serious crimes, and only with a warrant.
Police can use facial recognition in any criminal investigation.
Police can use facial recognition in any investigation, including scanning crowds live in public places.
facial_recognition_cases: Police shouldn't be able to use facial recognition for this: {case}.
Police should be able to use facial recognition for this: {case}.
data_privacy_law: A strict federal law should require companies to get your permission before collecting or selling your data.
A federal law should let you tell companies not to sell your data.
There shouldn't be a federal data privacy law; states should decide.
There shouldn't be any new data privacy laws; people can choose which services to use.
gov_buys_data: Government agencies should never buy people's personal data, like location history, without a warrant.
Agencies can buy personal data without a warrant only for national security investigations.
Agencies can buy any personal data that companies sell to anyone, without a warrant.
digital_id: There shouldn't be a national digital ID; state IDs and passports are enough.
There should be a federal digital ID on your phone, but only for people who want one.
Everyone should be required to have a federal digital ID.
border_device_search: Border agents should need a warrant to search anyone's phone or laptop, including citizens coming home.
Border agents should need reasonable suspicion of a crime to search a traveler's devices.
Border agents should be able to search any traveler's devices, as current rules mostly allow.
dna_databases: Police should never search consumer DNA sites to find suspects through their relatives.
Police can search consumer DNA sites only for violent crimes, and only with a warrant.
Police can search consumer DNA sites for violent crimes without a warrant.
Police can search consumer DNA sites to solve any crime.
workplace_monitoring: Employers can monitor workers' computers, keystrokes and locations only with the worker's agreement, for specific reasons.
Employers can monitor workers during work hours, but must tell them exactly what's being monitored.
Employers can monitor workers freely on company devices and time.
